name: NAS-Bench-MR
description: This work explores how to design a single neural network capable of adapting to multiple heterogeneous vision tasks, such as image segmentation, 3D detection, and video recognition. This goal is challenging because both network architecture search (NAS) spaces and methods in different tasks are inconsistent. We solve this challenge from both sides. We first introduce a unified design space for multiple tasks and build a multitask NAS benchmark (NAS-Bench-MR) on many widely used datasets, including ImageNet, Cityscapes, KITTI, and HMDB51. We further propose Network Coding Propagation (NCP), which back-propagates gradients of neural predictors to directly update architecture codes along the desired gradient directions to solve various tasks. In this way, optimal architecture configurations can be found by NCP in our large search space in seconds. reputation: A specialized NAS benchmark for multi-task vision that is well known in the architecture search literature but not a mainstream end-task benchmark.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; results are task- and dataset-specific across ImageNet, Cityscapes, KITTI, and HMDB51. Primarily used to compare architecture search methods rather than final application models.
